answer: Each epoch, identities post a 55-credit keyed bond and are assigned by randomness to one bank of a river, published at the wharf; no identity chooses its bank. At the horizon, the bank with more work wins under lantern audit: winners keep their bonds; losers forfeit 30 credits, burned. The k-th fake needs its bond, fee, and one-in-two forfeit chance, so 1,000 fakes lock 55,000 credits, pay 10,000 in fees, and lose 15,000 per epoch. Bought assignments fail; mirrored work burns both bonds, since each bank's work carries its own pigment seal. Honest agents pay 55 credits once.
